title: Infection and Response
seo_title: Year 10 Science: Infection and Response Worksheets (GCSE Combined Science)
standard_text: Communicable diseases caused by viruses, bacteria, fungi and protists, how they are spread and how their spread can be reduced; non-specific defences and the immune system; vaccination; antibiotics and painkillers; antibiotic resistance; the discovery and development of drugs, including clinical trials.
meta_desc: Free Year 10 GCSE Combined Science worksheets on infection and response: pathogens and diseases, the body's defences, white blood cells, vaccination, antibiotics, resistance and drug trials. 100 questions with answers.
key_sub: White blood cells engulf pathogens and make antibodies and antitoxins.
body_html:
How to think about it

Pathogens are microorganisms that cause disease.

  • Viruses damage cells from inside; bacteria may make toxins; fungi and protists cause diseases such as rose black spot and malaria.
  • The body's defences: skin, mucus, cilia, stomach acid, then white blood cells (phagocytosis, antibodies, antitoxins).
  • Vaccines give immunity without illness. Antibiotics kill bacteria only; overuse leads to resistance.
Example

Bacteria double every 20 min. After 1 hour from 1?

3 divisions

2 × 2 × 2

Answer: 8

Example

Measles: pathogen type?

Spread by droplets

Answer: a virus

Common mistakes

  • Thinking antibiotics kill viruses.
  • Thinking vaccines contain antibodies.
  • Thinking painkillers cure diseases.

faq.q: What is the difference between viruses and bacteria?
faq.a: Viruses are much smaller and reproduce inside cells, damaging them. Bacteria are living cells that can reproduce on their own and may make toxins. Antibiotics only work on bacteria.
A vaccine contains dead or inactive pathogens. White blood cells make antibodies and memory cells, so if the real pathogen enters, the body responds quickly.

faq.q: Why is antibiotic resistance a problem?
faq.a: Some bacteria survive antibiotics and reproduce, so resistant strains such as MRSA spread and become harder to treat.
